summary.intent: Debug why the FUSE-mounted folder shows stale file content after editing a file in the web UI, and fix the issue.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified in `crates/fuse/src/inode.rs` — `populate_folder()` never re-resolved already-resolved files even when `modified_at` changed. Fix applied, tests pass, committed to a `fix/` branch with PR created.

repo: FUSE mount folder metadata refreshes every 30s via TTL expiry; `drain_refresh_completions` calls `populate_folder` with new metadata after each refresh cycle.
Content cache is keyed by CID (content-addressed), so stale content was not a cache invalidation problem — the bug was upstream: the stale CID reference was never updated.
IPNS private key and encrypted key hex do not change when a file is edited — only the CID changes, so those fields can be preserved when re-marking a file for re-resolution.
The project uses a monorepo structure with a Rust FUSE crate (`crates/fuse`), a Tauri desktop app, a web UI, and a new Astro landing page — all recently pulled in a large merge (8796 insertions).

code.finding: `populate_folder()` preserved existing `InodeKind` wholesale for already-resolved files (`file_meta_resolved: true`), never comparing `modified_at` timestamps. Fix adds a timestamp comparison and resets to unresolved state when the incoming `modified_at` is newer, triggering fresh IPNS resolution on the next drain cycle.

workflow: Subagent-based debugging (gsd-debugger) kept the main context lean while the investigation consumed heavy file reads and hypothesis testing.
Spurious Cargo.lock diffs can appear after `cargo check` without any Cargo.toml version changes — worth reverting before committing to avoid noise in PRs.
The checkpoint/continuation pattern (agent pauses at human-verify, user confirms, fresh agent spawned with prior state) worked well for a fix that needed human verification before finalizing.

friction: Cargo.lock picked up a phantom version bump for `cipherbox-fuse` after `cargo check`, requiring a manual revert before committing.
open_items: The fix requires waiting ~30-60s for the metadata TTL cycle before the updated file appears in the mount — no mechanism exists to force immediate re-resolution after a detected edit.
Human verification of the fix in a live environment (build desktop app, run through the full upload→edit→verify flow) was deferred to the user.
